alignments.note: Waw rendered by the concessive connective *though* (rule 14, open list).
Demonstrative → *these*.
Numeral in construct → *three*, the chain rendered attributively (rule 28).
Article on אֲנָשִׁים; the phrase's one determiner is *these*, licensed by the written demonstrative (rule 41's limit).
Noun → *men*.
Agreement article on the demonstrative (rules 29, 47).

CORRECTED. בְּתוֹךְ is rendered by the single English word *in*, so rule 30 fuses preposition and construct noun on the same terms as בְּיַד → *by*, headed on the lexeme-bearing תָּוֶךְ; the verbless clause's supplied copula *were* joins that unit under rules 49 and 30 (לִפְנֵי → *was before*). The accepted reading gave *in* to בְּ alone and left תָּוֶךְ `unrepresented`, which rule 30 rejects where the one-English-word condition holds.
Suffix → *it* (rule 18).
The oath formula חַי־אָנִי is written *As I live*; the adjective takes *As … live*, discontinuous around the pronoun and headed on *live* (rule 55).
Explicit pronoun takes only its own *I*.
נְאֻם → *saith*.
Supplied *the* belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rule 15).
The suffix of אֲדֹנָי is not separately rendered (rule 22).
Divine name → *Jehovah*.
Verb with subject pronoun and modal; head on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24).
The written negative takes the opening correlative *neither*, the morpheme that is itself what that word says (rule 14).
Noun → *sons*.
Waw takes the closing correlative *nor* (rule 14).
Noun → *daughters*.
כִּי rendered by the connective *but* (rules 14, 35).
Independent pronoun → *they*.

CORRECTED. לְבַד is rendered by the single English word *only* and fuses under rule 30, headed on the lexeme-bearing בַּד; the suffix is no longer inside this unit, because the ASV spends a second English word, *themselves*, on that morpheme in particular, which is exactly what rule 30 says defeats the one-English-word condition for a morpheme.

CORRECTED. The 3mp suffix of לְבַדָּם takes the ASV's *themselves*, the pronoun that realizes it (rule 18); the unit is discontinuous from *only* under rule 25. The accepted alignment kept *themselves* with the Niphal as a voice rendering under rule 44, but the passive voice is already carried by *should be delivered*, so the reflexive is not what renders it; the alternative to this reading is `added` under rule 30, which is ruled out because a 3mp morpheme stands in the clause to license the word.
Niphal with its supplied modal and passive copula; head on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24).

review_notes: Corrected twice: בְּתוֹכָהּ → *were in it* now fuses בְּ+תוֹךְ to *were in* under rule 30 with the copula on that unit (rule 49); and *themselves* moves from the passive verb to the suffix of לְבַדָּם, which is the 3mp morpheme that licenses it (rule 18).
*neither … nor* is split between the written לֹא and the waw, as rule 14 directs when a present negative can carry the opening correlative.
Unlike EZK.14.16, the ASV writes a second English word for לְבַדָּם here, so rule 2 splits the expression instead of fusing all three morphemes.
